reflection.text:
This was a CORRECT call (Truth: Actin disruptors, Submitted: Actin disruptors, p=0.72) that is now unblinded as cytochalasin B (CID 5311281, name and BBBC021 structure agree, e16/e17). The reflection is still useful because several signals pointed away from actin and required explicit resolution.

What the evidence got right:

The quantitative actin and morphology signals were decisive and dose-consistent. Sampling was tiered: mid dose 1 uM (w_9c437e9416, e2) already showed cell_area z=-8.4 and frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+8.4 with tub_mean z=+7.5, low dose 0.1 uM (w_e7e6180a98, e7) showed the same direction (cell_area -4.1, multinucleate +3.4, cell_nuc_area_ratio -3.0), and high doses 3 uM (w_d7217e9f72, e8) and 10 uM (w_b9f2cbcfb2, e3) showed extreme actin texture/intensity changes (e3: act_glcm_contrast z=+36.0, tub_mean +27.7, tub_std +23.0; e8: tub_mean +31.3, act_mean +27.6, nuc_solidity -27.9). This triad - reduced spread area, cytokinesis-failure multinucleation, and punctate/high-contrast actin - is the classic cytochalasin phenotype.

The comparison to reference atlas got this right despite noise. Initial NSC 2/2 Actin disruptors (e4) and final NSC 3/4 Actin disruptors (e9) with summed similarity 1.812 vs 0.149 for the single DNA replication outlier at 0.1 uM (similarity 0.149) correctly prioritized the 1-NN majority vote per Ljosa et al. 2013 protocol over the noisier k-neighbour vote that favored Protein synthesis 4/10 then 6/10, Actin 3/10 (e4, e9). Dose-response trends over the 4 acquired wells were directionally correct (rho=+0.80 for multinucleate e10, rho=-0.80 for cell_area e11, rho=+0.80 for tub_mean e12) and rho=-0.20 for frac_large_nucleus e13 helped deprioritize Aurora kinase inhibitors which would predict large nuclei.

Mechanistically this aligns with the unblinded literature: cytochalasin B is an actin filament barbed-end capper that inhibits elongation, PMID 574873, with structural capping/severing observations PMID 40658853 and differential interference with actin-binding proteins described for cytochalasin B PMID 40914162, reviewed for cytochalasans PMID 37627312 and for cytochalasin/phalloidin effects on actin PMID 3312229. No clinical implication is inferred; this is an in vitro profiling result.

What misled / what I missed:

1. Tubulin signal was a misleading proxy. The very large tub_mean z-scores (+7.5 to +31.3, e2,e3,e8) plus tub_std +23.0 could be read as Microtubule stabilizers. This was explicitly in the microscopist differential (e6: Eg5, Aurora, Microtubule stabilizers) and in my hypothesis board as Microtubule stabilizers 0.04. In retrospect this was secondary to cell compaction/loss of spread area and increased fluor density, not primary tubulin polymerization.

2. Microscopy description alone was contested. e5 (density similar vs DMSO, candidates Aurora) and e6 (density lower vs DMSO, candidates Eg5/Aurora/Microtubule stabilizers) did not propose actin and would have misled if taken alone. This was why acquiring the high-dose quantitative actin texture channel (e3, e8) and NSC were necessary acquisition choices.

3. Statistical power was missed in design. I ran dose_response on only 4 wells/4 doses, yielding p=0.2 for the +0.80 rhos and p=0.8 for the large-nucleus test (e10-e13). The trends were correct but I did not acquire additional intermediate doses/replicates to make the test significant. The review critique correctly flags this as a CONTESTED datum problem: e9 processes only 4 of 8 available doses, and the 3/4 majority hinges partly on dose index 5 (3 uM, similarity 0.628). A fuller 6-8 well titration would have resolved the low-dose DNA replication outlier and made rho significant.

4. Literature queries were too narrow initially (e18,e19,e21 returned 0 hits) before broadening to 'cytochalasin actin filament' which returned the 5 relevant PMIDs (e20). I should have started broader and cited the capping mechanism during hypothesis updating rather than after unblinding.

Why the acquisition choices worked: sampling 1 uM then 10 uM early (e2,e3) captured the active range; adding 0.1 uM (e7) and 3 uM (e8) confirmed onset and escalation before the second NSC. This outweighed the protein synthesis k-neighbour signal and the antimitotic microscopy suggestions. Final hypothesis Actin 0.68 (e14) was appropriately dominant but not overstated, matching the final protocol tally.

Next improvement is exactly what was proposed: high-resolution single-channel phalloidin/tubulin immunofluorescence with titration and washout plus live cytokinesis timelapse, to directly test punctate actin aggregates, loss of stress fibers, reduced area, and reversibility versus a reference actin disruptor at matched doses.
